summary.tldr: Sets rules for Gatineau Park, including fixed boundaries, ecological protection, limits on public land sales, and new consultation and regulation powers.
what_it_does: Sets Gatineau Park’s boundaries in a new schedule, and lets the Governor in Council enlarge the park if the federal government has title to the land.
Makes ecological integrity the National Capital Commission’s first priority when managing the park, and requires a long-term master plan within 10 years and every 10 years after that.

Prohibits selling or giving away public lands in the park, except for certain transfers to Algonquin Anishinabeg bodies or public authorities for health care, social services, culture, or public infrastructure.
Requires the Commission to provide public participation and to consult nearby municipalities and Algonquin Anishinabeg governing bodies, with the consultations reported on its website.
Allows regulations on park activities, permits, fees, and ecological integrity, and says fees cannot be higher than the Commission’s cost.
Allows the Minister to designate enforcement officers and to set summary conviction penalties for breaking park regulations.
who_it_affects: Businesses and workers in the region
Public land users in the park
summary.background: The bill amends the National Capital Act and adds a new schedule that describes Gatineau Park’s boundaries.
